name: Mémorial Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza
subtitle: Monumental mausoleum along the Congo River preserving the remains of the city's founder and historic documentation.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Overlooking the banks of the Congo River in central Brazzaville

facts.label: Significance
facts.value: Houses the crypt of Pietro Savorgnan di Brazzà and his family, commemorating the 1880 treaty with Makoko Illoy I

parts.text: A prominent civic memorial and marble mausoleum overlooking the vast waters of the Congo River. Inaugurated in October 2006, it houses the crypt of the Italian-born French explorer Pietro Savorgnan di Brazzà, whose remains, along with those of his wife and four children, were repatriated from Algiers to Brazzaville. The site preserves historical documents, treaties, and bas-relief murals depicting the peaceful pact negotiated in 1880 between Brazza and the Bateke monarch King Makoko Illoy I, which marked the founding of the capital.
